fix(text): truncate fits a wider marker to the width (rich-text-odh) (#218)

* fix(text): truncate fits a wider marker to the width (rich-text-odh)

truncate(width, { marker }) returned the marker whole when it was wider
than width, so truncate(1, { marker: ">>" }) drew two cells. The marker is
now cut to the width as a value, and the kept-text budget is what the
fitted marker leaves; the width <= 0 early return is subsumed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cells): cellFit cuts between grapheme clusters (rich-text-odh)

cellFit summed cellLen per code point, while cellLen measures clusters,
so a VS16 or ZWJ marker was "fitted" wider than the width (❤️ at 1 cell)
or cut mid-glyph (👨‍👩‍👧 at 4). truncate's own text crops had the same
walk. Both now go through graphemes() + fitClusters in cells.ts, and
export-html's private segmenter is that same one.

The remaining per-code-point walkers are rich-cells-1y9d.

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(table): draw with Table.style and Column's three styles, as the reference does (rich-table-jph)

Table.style is the base the border style layers over; a column's headerStyle and
footerStyle layer over the table's, and its style sits under the row's rowStyles
entry. The cell's style now covers its padding and the blank lines a short cell
runs out of, which is where the reference puts it. Each case is pinned against
Python Rich 9d8f9a3's bytes.
